and wired accordingly to Sir James. He’s booked rooms for us, and will
be round to dine at eight.”"}, {"paragraph": 2, "text": "“What made you think he’d ceased to take any interest in the case?”
 asked Tommy curiously."}, {"paragraph": 3, "text": "“What he said,” replied Julius dryly. “The old bird’s as close as an

You bet your life it was.”"}, {"paragraph": 9, "text": "Tommy shook his head unconvinced."}, {"paragraph": 10, "text": "Sir James arrived punctually at eight o’clock, and Julius introduced
Tommy. Sir James shook hands with him warmly."}, {"paragraph": 11, "text": "“I am delighted to make your acquaintance, Mr. Beresford. I have heard
so much about you from Miss Tuppence”--he smiled involuntarily--“that it
really seems as though I already know you quite well.”"}, {"paragraph": 12, "text": "“Thank you, sir,” said Tommy with his cheerful grin. He scanned the
great lawyer eagerly. Like Tuppence, he felt the magnetism of the
other’s personality. He was reminded of Mr. Carter. The two men, totally
unlike so far as physical resemblance went, produced a similar effect.
Beneath the weary manner of the one and the professional reserve of the
other, lay the same quality of mind, keen-edged like a rapier."}, {"paragraph": 13, "text": "In the meantime he was conscious of Sir James’s close scrutiny. When the
lawyer dropped his eyes the young man had the feeling that the other had
read him through and through like an open book. He could not but wonder
what the final judgment was, but there was little chance of learning
that. Sir James took in everything, but gave out only what he chose. A
proof of that occurred almost at once."}, {"paragraph": 14, "text": "Immediately the first greetings were over Julius broke out into a flood
of eager questions. How had Sir James managed to track the girl? Why had
he not let them know that he was still working on the case? And so on."}, {"paragraph": 15, "text": "Sir James stroked his chin and smiled. At last he said:"}, {"paragraph": 16, "text": "“Just so, just so. Well, she’s found. And that’s the great thing, isn’t
it? Eh! Come now, that’s the great thing?”"}, {"paragraph": 17, "text": "“Sure it is. But just how did you strike her trail? Miss Tuppence and I
thought you’d quit for good and all.”"}, {"paragraph": 18, "text": "“Ah!” The lawyer shot a lightning glance at him, then resumed operations
on his chin. “You thought that, did you? Did you really? H’m, dear me.”"}, {"paragraph": 19, "text": "“But I guess I can take it we were wrong,” pursued Julius."}, {"paragraph": 20, "text": "“Well, I don’t know that I should go so far as to say that. But it’s
certainly fortunate for all parties that we’ve managed to find the young
lady.”"}, {"paragraph": 21, "text": "“But where is she?” demanded Julius, his thoughts flying off on another
tack. “I thought you’d be sure to bring her along?”"}, {"paragraph": 22, "text": "“That would hardly be possible,” said Sir James gravely."}, {"paragraph": 23, "text": "“Why?”"}, {"paragraph": 24, "text": "“Because the young lady was knocked down in a street accident, and has
sustained slight injuries to the head. She was taken to the infirmary,
and on recovering consciousness gave her name as Jane Finn. When--ah!--I
heard that, I arranged for her to be removed to the house of a
doctor--a friend of mine, and wired at once for you. She relapsed into
unconsciousness and has not spoken since.”"}, {"paragraph": 25, "text": "“She’s not seriously hurt?”"}, {"paragraph": 26, "text": "“Oh, a bruise and a cut or two; really, from a medical point of view,
absurdly slight injuries to have produced such a condition. Her state is
probably to be attributed to the mental shock consequent on recovering
her memory.”"}, {"paragraph": 27, "text": "“It’s come back?” cried Julius excitedly."}, {"paragraph": 28, "text": "Sir James tapped the table rather impatiently."}, {"paragraph": 29, "text": "“Undoubtedly, Mr. Hersheimmer, since she was able to give her real name.
I thought you had appreciated that point.”"}, {"paragraph": 30, "text": "“And you just happened to be on the spot,” said Tommy. “Seems quite like
a fairy tale.”"}, {"paragraph": 31, "text": "But Sir James was far too wary to be drawn."}, {"paragraph": 32, "text": "“Coincidences are curious things,” he said dryly."}, {"paragraph": 33, "text": "Nevertheless Tommy was now certain of what he had before only suspected.
Sir James’s presence in Manchester was not accidental. Far from
abandoning the case, as Julius supposed, he had by some means of his own
successfully run the missing girl to earth. The only thing that puzzled
Tommy was the reason for all this secrecy. He concluded that it was a
foible of the legal mind."}, {"paragraph": 34, "text": "Julius was speaking."}, {"paragraph": 35, "text": "“After dinner,” he announced, “I shall go right away and see Jane.”"}, {"paragraph": 36, "text": "“That will be impossible, I fear,” said Sir James. “It is very unlikely
they would allow her to see visitors at this time of night. I should
suggest to-morrow morning about ten o’clock.”"}, {"paragraph": 37, "text": "Julius flushed. There was something in Sir James which always stirred
him to antagonism. It was a conflict of two masterful personalities."}, {"paragraph": 38, "text": "“All the same, I reckon I’ll go round there to-night and see if I can’t
ginger them up to break through their silly rules.”"}, {"paragraph": 39, "text": "“It will be quite useless, Mr. Hersheimmer.”"}, {"paragraph": 40, "text": "The words came out like the crack of a pistol, and Tommy looked up with
a start. Julius was nervous and excited. The hand with which he raised
his glass to his lips shook slightly, but his eyes held Sir James’s
defiantly. For a moment the hostility between the two seemed likely to
burst into flame, but in the end Julius lowered his eyes, defeated."}, {"paragraph": 41, "text": "“For the moment, I reckon you’re the boss.”"}, {"paragraph": 42, "text": "“Thank you,” said the other. “We will say ten o’clock then?” With
consummate ease of manner he turned to Tommy. “I must confess, Mr.
Beresford, that it was something of a surprise to me to see you here
this evening. The last I heard of you was that your friends were in
grave anxiety on your behalf. Nothing had been heard of you for
some days, and Miss Tuppence was inclined to think you had got into
difficulties.”"}, {"paragraph": 43, "text": "“I had, sir!” Tommy grinned reminiscently. “I was never in a tighter
place in my life.”"}, {"paragraph": 44, "text": "Helped out by questions from Sir James, he gave an abbreviated account
of his adventures. The lawyer looked at him with renewed interest as he
brought the tale to a close."}, {"paragraph": 45, "text": "“You got yourself out of a tight place very well,” he said gravely. “I
congratulate you. You displayed a great deal of ingenuity and carried
your part through well.”"}, {"paragraph": 46, "text": "Tommy blushed, his face assuming a prawnlike hue at the praise."}, {"paragraph": 47, "text": "“I couldn’t have got away but for the girl, sir.”"}, {"paragraph": 48, "text": "“No.” Sir James smiled a little. “It was lucky for you she happened
to--er--take a fancy to you.” Tommy appeared about to protest, but Sir
James went on. “There’s no doubt about her being one of the gang, I
suppose?”"}, {"paragraph": 49, "text": "“I’m afraid not, sir. I thought perhaps they were keeping her there by
force, but the way she acted didn’t fit in with that. You see, she went
back to them when she could have got away.”"}, {"paragraph": 50, "text": "Sir James nodded thoughtfully."}, {"paragraph": 51, "text": "“What did she say? Something about wanting to be taken to Marguerite?”"}, {"paragraph": 52, "text": "“Yes, sir. I suppose she meant Mrs. Vandemeyer.”"}, {"paragraph": 53, "text": "“She always signed herself Rita Vandemeyer. All her friends spoke of
her as Rita. Still, I suppose the girl must have been in the habit of
calling her by her full name. And, at the moment she was crying out to
her, Mrs. Vandemeyer was either dead or dying! Curious! There are one
or two points that strike me as being obscure--their sudden change
of attitude towards yourself, for instance. By the way, the house was
raided, of course?”"}, {"paragraph": 54, "text": "“Yes, sir, but they’d all cleared out.”"}, {"paragraph": 55, "text": "“Naturally,” said Sir James dryly."}, {"paragraph": 56, "text": "“And not a clue left behind.”"}, {"paragraph": 57, "text": "“I wonder----” The lawyer tapped the table thoughtfully."}, {"paragraph": 58, "text": "Something in his voice made Tommy look up. Would this man’s eyes have
seen something where theirs had been blind? He spoke impulsively:"}, {"paragraph": 59, "text": "“I wish you’d been there, sir, to go over the house!”"}, {"paragraph": 60, "text": "“I wish I had,” said Sir James quietly. He sat for a moment in silence.
Then he looked up. “And since then? What have you been doing?”"}, {"paragraph": 61, "text": "For a moment, Tommy stared at him. Then it dawned on him that of course
the lawyer did not know."}, {"paragraph": 62, "text": "“I forgot that you didn’t know about Tuppence,” he said slowly. The
sickening anxiety, forgotten for a while in the excitement of knowing
Jane Finn was found at last, swept over him again."}, {"paragraph": 63, "text": "The lawyer laid down his knife and fork sharply."}, {"paragraph": 64, "text": "“Has anything happened to Miss Tuppence?” His voice was keen-edged."}, {"paragraph": 65, "text": "“She’s disappeared,” said Julius."}, {"paragraph": 66, "text": "“When?”"}, {"paragraph": 67, "text": "“A week ago.”"}, {"paragraph": 68, "text": "“How?”"}, {"paragraph": 69, "text": "Sir James’s questions fairly shot out. Between them Tommy and Julius
gave the history of the last week and their futile search."}, {"paragraph": 70, "text": "Sir James went at once to the root of the matter."}, {"paragraph": 71, "text": "“A wire signed with your name? They knew enough of you both for that.
They weren’t sure of how much you had learnt in that house. Their
kidnapping of Miss Tuppence is the counter-move to your escape. If
necessary they could seal your lips with a threat of what might happen
to her.”"}, {"paragraph": 72, "text": "Tommy nodded."}, {"paragraph": 73, "text": "“That’s just what I thought, sir.”"}, {"paragraph": 74, "text": "Sir James looked at him keenly. “You had worked that out, had you? Not
bad--not at all bad. The curious thing is that they certainly did not
know anything about you when they first held you prisoner. You are sure
that you did not in any way disclose your identity?”"}, {"paragraph": 75, "text": "Tommy shook his head."}, {"paragraph": 76, "text": "“That’s so,” said Julius with a nod. “Therefore I reckon some one put
them wise--and not earlier than Sunday afternoon.”"}, {"paragraph": 77, "text": "“Yes, but who?”"}, {"paragraph": 78, "text": "“That almighty omniscient Mr. Brown, of course!”"}, {"paragraph": 79, "text": "There was a faint note of derision in the American’s voice which made
Sir James look up sharply."}, {"paragraph": 80, "text": "“You don’t believe in Mr. Brown, Mr. Hersheimmer?”"}, {"paragraph": 81, "text": "“No, sir, I do not,” returned the young American with emphasis. “Not
as such, that is to say. I reckon it out that he’s a figurehead--just a
bogy name to frighten the children with. The real head of this business
is that Russian chap Kramenin. I guess he’s quite capable of running
revolutions in three countries at once if he chose! The man Whittington
is probably the head of the English branch.”"}, {"paragraph": 82, "text": "“I disagree with you,” said Sir James shortly. “Mr. Brown exists.” He
turned to Tommy. “Did you happen to notice where that wire was handed
in?”"}, {"paragraph": 83, "text": "“No, sir, I’m afraid I didn’t.”"}, {"paragraph": 84, "text": "“H’m. Got it with you?”"}, {"paragraph": 85, "text": "“It’s upstairs, sir, in my kit.”"}, {"paragraph": 86, "text": "“I’d like to have a look at it sometime. No hurry. You’ve wasted a
week”--Tommy hung his head--“a day or so more is immaterial. We’ll deal
with Miss Jane Finn first. Afterwards, we’ll set to work to rescue Miss
Tuppence from bondage. I don’t think she’s in any immediate danger. That
is, so long as they don’t know that we’ve got Jane Finn, and that
her memory has returned. We must keep that dark at all costs. You
understand?”"}, {"paragraph": 87, "text": "The other two assented, and, after making arrangements for meeting on
the morrow, the great lawyer took his leave."}, {"paragraph": 88, "text": "At ten o’clock, the two young men were at the appointed spot. Sir
James had joined them on the doorstep. He alone appeared unexcited. He
introduced them to the doctor."}, {"paragraph": 89, "text": "“Mr. Hersheimmer--Mr. Beresford--Dr. Roylance. How’s the patient?”"}, {"paragraph": 90, "text": "“Going on well. Evidently no idea of the flight of time. Asked this
morning how many had been saved from the _Lusitania_. Was it in the
papers yet? That, of course, was only what was to be expected. She seems
to have something on her mind, though.”"}, {"paragraph": 91, "text": "“I think we can relieve her anxiety. May we go up?”"}, {"paragraph": 92, "text": "“Certainly.”"}, {"paragraph": 93, "text": "Tommy’s heart beat sensibly faster as they followed the doctor upstairs.
Jane Finn at last! The long-sought, the mysterious, the elusive Jane
Finn! How wildly improbable success had seemed! And here in this house,
her memory almost miraculously restored, lay the girl who held the
future of England in her hands. A half groan broke from Tommy’s lips.
If only Tuppence could have been at his side to share in the triumphant
conclusion of their joint venture! Then he put the thought of Tuppence
resolutely aside. His confidence in Sir James was growing. There was
a man who would unerringly ferret out Tuppence’s whereabouts. In the
meantime Jane Finn! And suddenly a dread clutched at his heart. It
seemed too easy.... Suppose they should find her dead ... stricken down
by the hand of Mr. Brown?"}, {"paragraph": 94, "text": "In another minute he was laughing at these melodramatic fancies. The
doctor held open the door of a room and they passed in. On the white
bed, bandages round her head, lay the girl. Somehow the whole scene
seemed unreal. It was so exactly what one expected that it gave the
effect of being beautifully staged."}, {"paragraph": 95, "text": "The girl looked from one to the other of them with large wondering eyes.
Sir James spoke first."}, {"paragraph": 96, "text": "“Miss Finn,” he said, “this is your cousin, Mr. Julius P. Hersheimmer.”"}, {"paragraph": 97, "text": "A faint flush flitted over the girl’s face, as Julius stepped forward
and took her hand."}, {"paragraph": 98, "text": "“How do, Cousin Jane?” he said lightly."}, {"paragraph": 99, "text": "But Tommy caught the tremor in his voice."}, {"paragraph": 100, "text": "“Are you really Uncle Hiram’s son?” she asked wonderingly."}, {"paragraph": 101, "text": "Her voice, with the slight warmth of the Western accent, had an almost
thrilling quality. It seemed vaguely familiar to Tommy, but he thrust
the impression aside as impossible."}, {"paragraph": 102, "text": "“Sure thing.”"}, {"paragraph": 103, "text": "“We used to read about Uncle Hiram in the papers,” continued the girl,
in her low soft tones. “But I never thought I’d meet you one day. Mother
figured it out that Uncle Hiram would never get over being mad with
her.”"}, {"paragraph": 104, "text": "“The old man was like that,” admitted Julius. “But I guess the new
generation’s sort of different. Got no use for the family feud business.
First thing I thought about, soon as the war was over, was to come along
and hunt you up.”"}, {"paragraph": 105, "text": "A shadow passed over the girl’s face."}, {"paragraph": 106, "text": "“They’ve been telling me things--dreadful things--that my memory went,
and that there are years I shall never know about--years lost out of my
life.”"}, {"paragraph": 107, "text": "“You didn’t realize that yourself?”"}, {"paragraph": 108, "text": "The girl’s eyes opened wide."}, {"paragraph": 109, "text": "“Why, no. It seems to me as though it were no time since we were being
hustled into those boats. I can see it all now.” She closed her eyes
with a shudder."}, {"paragraph": 110, "text": "Julius looked across at Sir James, who nodded."}, {"paragraph": 111, "text": "“Don’t worry any. It isn’t worth it. Now, see here, Jane, there’s
something we want to know about. There was a man aboard that boat with
some mighty important papers on him, and the big guns in this country
have got a notion that he passed on the goods to you. Is that so?”"}, {"paragraph": 112, "text": "The girl hesitated, her glance shifting to the other two. Julius
understood."}, {"paragraph": 113, "text": "“Mr. Beresford is commissioned by the British Government to get those
papers back. Sir James Peel Edgerton is an English Member of Parliament,
and might be a big gun in the Cabinet if he liked. It’s owing to him

Do you reckon there was a dictaphone in Jane’s room?”"}, {"paragraph": 6, "text": "But Tommy’s common sense pointed out objections."}, {"paragraph": 7, "text": "“No one could have known beforehand that she was going to be in that house--much less that particular room.”"}, {"paragraph": 8, "text": "“I wish that chap Peel Edgerton had been with us,” said Tommy thoughtfully."}, {"paragraph": 9, "text": "“Why?” Julius stared. “The mischief was done when we came.”"}, {"paragraph": 10, "text": "“Yes----” Tommy hesitated. He could not explain his own feeling--the illogical idea that the K.C.’s presence would somehow have averted the catastrophe. “The game’s up. I must get back to London. Mr. Carter must be warned.”"}, {"paragraph": 11, "text": "He took the midnight mail to London. Julius elected to stay the night at Holyhead."}, {"paragraph": 12, "text": "Half an hour after arrival, Tommy stood before his chief."}, {"paragraph": 13, "text": "“I’ve come to report, sir. I’ve failed--failed badly.”"}, {"paragraph": 14, "text": "“Ah!” said Mr. Carter quietly. The expression on his face did not change, but Tommy caught the flicker of despair in his eyes."}, {"paragraph": 15, "text": "Through Tommy’s mind flashed the assurance: “It’s hopeless, and he knows it’s hopeless!”"}, {"paragraph": 16, "text": "“Don’t take it to heart, lad,” Mr. Carter said kindly. “You did your best. And you came very near success. I blame myself. I have been blaming myself ever since I heard this other news.”"}, {"paragraph": 17, "text": "A new fear gripped at Tommy’s heart. Mr. Carter stretched out his hand to a sheet on the table."}, {"paragraph": 18, "text": "“Tuppence----?” faltered Tommy."}, {"paragraph": 19, "text": "“Read for yourself.”"}, {"paragraph": 20, "text": "The typewritten words danced before his eyes. The description of a green toque, a coat with a handkerchief in the pocket marked P.L.C."}, {"paragraph": 21, "text": "“Washed up on the Yorkshire coast--near Ebury. I’m afraid--it looks very much like foul play.”"}, {"paragraph": 22, "text": "“My God!” gasped Tommy. “_Tuppence!_ Those devils--I’ll never rest till I’ve got even with them! I’ll----”"}, {"paragraph": 23, "text": "The pity on Mr. Carter’s face stopped him."}, {"paragraph": 24, "text": "“I know what you feel like, my poor boy. But it’s no good. Cut your losses. Time’s merciful. You’ll forget.”"}, {"paragraph": 25, "text": "“Forget Tuppence? Never!”"}, {"paragraph": 26, "text": "“There’s no need for you to blame yourself, sir,” Tommy said with an effort. “But I wish to God I’d been the one to get it in the neck. Good-bye, sir.”"}, {"paragraph": 27, "text": "Back at the _Ritz_, Tommy packed up his few belongings mechanically. _Tuppence--dead!_ Little Tuppence, brimming over with life!"}, {"paragraph": 28, "text": "They brought him a note, a few kind words of sympathy from Peel Edgerton, who had read the news in the paper. (There had been a large headline: EX-V.A.D. FEARED DROWNED.) The letter ended with the offer of a post on a ranch in the Argentine."}, {"paragraph": 29, "text": "The door opened, and Julius burst in with an open newspaper in his hand."}, {"paragraph": 30, "text": "“Say, what’s all this? They seem to have got some fool idea about Tuppence.”"}, {"paragraph": 31, "text": "“It’s true,” said Tommy quietly."}, {"paragraph": 32, "text": "“Well, I’m darned!” said Julius. “Little Tuppence. She sure was the pluckiest little girl----”"}, {"paragraph": 33, "text": "But suddenly something seemed to crack in Tommy’s brain."}, {"paragraph": 34, "text": "“Oh, get out! You don’t really care, damn you! You asked her to marry you in your rotten cold-blooded way, but I _loved_ her. I’d have given the soul out of my body to save her from harm.”"}, {"paragraph": 35, "text": "“See here,” began Julius temperately."}, {"paragraph": 36, "text": "“Oh, go to the devil! Go and look after your cousin. Tuppence is my girl! I shall never forget when I was in hospital, and she came in in that ridiculous cap and apron! It was like a miracle to see the girl I loved turn up in a nurse’s kit----”"}, {"paragraph": 37, "text": "But Julius interrupted him."}, {"paragraph": 38, "text": "“A nurse’s kit! Gee whiz! I could swear I’ve seen Jane in a nurse’s cap too. No, by gum, I’ve got it! It was her I saw talking to Whittington at that nursing home in Bournemouth. She wasn’t a patient there! She was a nurse!”"}, {"paragraph": 39, "text": "“I dare say,” said Tommy angrily, “she’s probably been in with them from the start.”"}, {"paragraph": 40, "text": "“I’m darned if she did!” shouted Julius. “She’s my cousin, and as patriotic a girl as ever stepped.”"}, {"paragraph": 41, "text": "The young men were on the point of coming to blows. But suddenly, with an almost magical abruptness, Julius’s anger abated."}, {"paragraph": 42, "text": "“All right, son,” he said quietly, “I’m going. I don’t blame you any for what you’ve been saying. It’s mighty lucky you did say it. I’ve been the most almighty blithering darned idiot that it’s possible to imagine. I’m going right away now--going to the London and North Western Railway depot, if you want to know.”"}, {"paragraph": 43, "text": "When the door closed, he finished packing and rang for his luggage to be taken down."}, {"paragraph": 44, "text": "“Going away, sir?”"}, {"paragraph": 45, "text": "“I’m going to the devil,” said Tommy."}, {"paragraph": 46, "text": "Beyond a fixed determination to get even with Mr. Brown he had no plans. Still, Sir James’s letter had been kind; better answer it. Finding no paper in his room, he remembered the good supply in Julius’s sitting-room. He was beginning to be rather ashamed of the things he had said. He’d apologize if he found him there."}, {"paragraph": 47, "text": "But the room was deserted. Tommy opened the middle drawer of the writing-table. A photograph, carelessly thrust in face upwards, caught his eye."}, {"paragraph": 48, "text": "What on earth was a photograph of the French girl Annette doing in Julius Hersheimmer’s writing-table?"}], "025.source": [{"paragraph": 1, "text": "IN his suite at Claridge’s, Kramenin reclined on a couch and dictated to
his secretary in sibilant Russian."}, {"paragraph": 2, "text": "Presently the telephone at the secretary’s elbow purred, and he took up
the receiver, spoke for a minute or two, then turned to his employer."}, {"paragraph": 3, "text": "“Some one below is asking for you.”"}, {"paragraph": 4, "text": "“Who is it?”"}, {"paragraph": 5, "text": "“He gives the name of Mr. Julius P. Hersheimmer.”"}, {"paragraph": 6, "text": "“Hersheimmer,” repeated Kramenin thoughtfully. “I have heard that name
before.”"}, {"paragraph": 7, "text": "“His father was one of the steel kings of America,” explained the
secretary, whose business it was to know everything. “This young man
must be a millionaire several times over.”"}, {"paragraph": 8, "text": "The other’s eyes narrowed appreciatively."}, {"paragraph": 9, "text": "“You had better go down and see him, Ivan. Find out what he wants.”"}, {"paragraph": 10, "text": "The secretary obeyed, closing the door noiselessly behind him. In a few
minutes he returned."}, {"paragraph": 11, "text": "“He declines to state his business--says it is entirely private and
personal, and that he must see you.”"}, {"paragraph": 12, "text": "“A millionaire several times over,” murmured Kramenin. “Bring him up, my
dear Ivan.”"}, {"paragraph": 13, "text": "The secretary left the room once more, and returned escorting Julius."}, {"paragraph": 14, "text": "“Monsieur Kramenin?” said the latter abruptly."}, {"paragraph": 15, "text": "The Russian, studying him attentively with his pale venomous eyes,
bowed."}, {"paragraph": 16, "text": "“Pleased to meet you,” said the American. “I’ve got some very important
business I’d like to talk over with you, if I can see you alone.” He
looked pointedly at the other."}, {"paragraph": 17, "text": "“My secretary, Monsieur Grieber, from whom I have no secrets.”"}, {"paragraph": 18, "text": "“That may be so--but I have,” said Julius dryly. “So I’d be obliged if
you’d tell him to scoot.”"}, {"paragraph": 19, "text": "“Ivan,” said the Russian softly, “perhaps you would not mind retiring
into the next room----”"}, {"paragraph": 20, "text": "“The next room won’t do,” interrupted Julius. “I know these ducal
suites--and I want this one plumb empty except for you and me. Send him
round to a store to buy a penn’orth of peanuts.”"}, {"paragraph": 21, "text": "Though not particularly enjoying the American’s free and easy manner
of speech, Kramenin was devoured by curiosity. “Will your business take
long to state?”"}, {"paragraph": 22, "text": "“Might be an all night job if you caught on.”"}, {"paragraph": 23, "text": "“Very good, Ivan. I shall not require you again this evening. Go to the
theatre--take a night off.”"}, {"paragraph": 24, "text": "“Thank you, your excellency.”"}, {"paragraph": 25, "text": "The secretary bowed and departed."}, {"paragraph": 26, "text": "Julius stood at the door watching his retreat. Finally, with a satisfied
sigh, he closed it, and came back to his position in the centre of the
room."}, {"paragraph": 27, "text": "“Now, Mr. Hersheimmer, perhaps you will be so kind as to come to the
point?”"}, {"paragraph": 28, "text": "“I guess that won’t take a minute,” drawled Julius. Then, with an abrupt
change of manner: “Hands up--or I shoot!”"}, {"paragraph": 29, "text": "For a moment Kramenin stared blindly into the big automatic, then, with
almost comical haste, he flung up his hands above his head. In that
instant Julius had taken his measure. The man he had to deal with was an
abject physical coward--the rest would be easy."}, {"paragraph": 30, "text": "“This is an outrage,” cried the Russian in a high hysterical voice. “An
outrage! Do you mean to kill me?”"}, {"paragraph": 31, "text": "“Not if you keep your voice down. Don’t go edging sideways towards that
bell. That’s better.”"}, {"paragraph": 32, "text": "“What do you want? Do nothing rashly. Remember my life is of the utmost
value to my country. I may have been maligned----”"}, {"paragraph": 33, "text": "“I reckon,” said Julius, “that the man who let daylight into you would
be doing humanity a good turn. But you needn’t worry any. I’m not
proposing to kill you this trip--that is, if you’re reasonable.”"}, {"paragraph": 34, "text": "The Russian quailed before the stern menace in the other’s eyes. He
passed his tongue over his dry lips."}, {"paragraph": 35, "text": "“What do you want? Money?”"}, {"paragraph": 36, "text": "“No. I want Jane Finn.”"}, {"paragraph": 37, "text": "“Jane Finn? I--never heard of her!”"}, {"paragraph": 38, "text": "“You’re a darned liar! You know perfectly who I mean.”"}, {"paragraph": 39, "text": "“I tell you I’ve never heard of the girl.”"}, {"paragraph": 40, "text": "“And I tell you,” retorted Julius, “that Little Willie here is just
hopping mad to go off!”"}, {"paragraph": 41, "text": "The Russian wilted visibly."}, {"paragraph": 42, "text": "“You wouldn’t dare----”"}, {"paragraph": 43, "text": "“Oh, yes, I would, son!”"}, {"paragraph": 44, "text": "Kramenin must have recognized something in the voice that carried
conviction, for he said sullenly:"}, {"paragraph": 45, "text": "“Well? Granted I do know who you mean--what of it?”"}, {"paragraph": 46, "text": "“You will tell me now--right here--where she is to be found.”"}, {"paragraph": 47, "text": "Kramenin shook his head."}, {"paragraph": 48, "text": "“I daren’t.”"}, {"paragraph": 49, "text": "“Why not?”"}, {"paragraph": 50, "text": "“I daren’t. You ask an impossibility.”"}, {"paragraph": 51, "text": "“Afraid, eh? Of whom? Mr. Brown? Ah, that tickles you up! There is such
a person, then? I doubted it. And the mere mention of him scares you
stiff!”"}, {"paragraph": 52, "text": "“I have seen him,” said the Russian slowly. “Spoken to him face to face.
I did not know it until afterwards. He was one of a crowd. I should not
know him again. Who is he really? I do not know. But I know this--he is
a man to fear.”"}, {"paragraph": 53, "text": "“He’ll never know,” said Julius."}, {"paragraph": 54, "text": "“He knows everything--and his vengeance is swift. Even
I--Kramenin!--would not be exempt!”"}, {"paragraph": 55, "text": "“Then you won’t do as I ask you?”"}, {"paragraph": 56, "text": "“You ask an impossibility.”"}, {"paragraph": 57, "text": "“Sure that’s a pity for you,” said Julius cheerfully. “But the world in
general will benefit.” He raised the revolver."}, {"paragraph": 58, "text": "“Stop,” shrieked the Russian. “You cannot mean to shoot me?”"}, {"paragraph": 59, "text": "“Of course I do. I’ve always heard you Revolutionists held life cheap,
but it seems there’s a difference when it’s your own life in question.
I gave you just one chance of saving your dirty skin, and that you
wouldn’t take!”"}, {"paragraph": 60, "text": "“They would kill me!”"}, {"paragraph": 61, "text": "“Well,” said Julius pleasantly, “it’s up to you. But I’ll just say this.
Little Willie here is a dead cert, and if I was you I’d take a sporting
chance with Mr. Brown!”"}, {"paragraph": 62, "text": "“You will hang if you shoot me,” muttered the Russian irresolutely."}, {"paragraph": 63, "text": "“No, stranger, that’s where you’re wrong. You forget the dollars. A
big crowd of solicitors will get busy, and they’ll get some high-brow
doctors on the job, and the end of it all will be that they’ll say my
brain was unhinged. I shall spend a few months in a quiet sanatorium, my
mental health will improve, the doctors will declare me sane again, and
all will end happily for little Julius. I guess I can bear a few months’
retirement in order to rid the world of you, but don’t you kid yourself
I’ll hang for it!”"}, {"paragraph": 64, "text": "The Russian believed him. Corrupt himself, he believed implicitly in the
power of money. He had read of American murder trials running much on
the lines indicated by Julius. He had bought and sold justice himself.
This virile young American, with the significant drawling voice, had the
whip hand of him."}, {"paragraph": 65, "text": "“I’m going to count five,” continued Julius, “and I guess, if you let me
get past four, you needn’t worry any about Mr. Brown. Maybe he’ll send
some flowers to the funeral, but _you_ won’t smell them! Are you ready?
I’ll begin. One--two--three--four----”"}, {"paragraph": 66, "text": "The Russian interrupted with a shriek:"}, {"paragraph": 67, "text": "“Do not shoot. I will do all you wish.”"}, {"paragraph": 68, "text": "Julius lowered the revolver."}, {"paragraph": 69, "text": "“I thought you’d hear sense. Where is the girl?”"}, {"paragraph": 70, "text": "“At Gatehouse, in Kent. Astley Priors, the place is called.”"}, {"paragraph": 71, "text": "“Is she a prisoner there?”"}, {"paragraph": 72, "text": "“She’s not allowed to leave the house--though it’s safe enough really.
The little fool has lost her memory, curse her!”"}, {"paragraph": 73, "text": "“That’s been annoying for you and your friends, I reckon. What about the
other girl, the one you decoyed away over a week ago?”"}, {"paragraph": 74, "text": "“She’s there too,” said the Russian sullenly."}, {"paragraph": 75, "text": "“That’s good,” said Julius. “Isn’t it all panning out beautifully? And a
lovely night for the run!”"}, {"paragraph": 76, "text": "“What run?” demanded Kramenin, with a stare."}, {"paragraph": 77, "text": "“Down to Gatehouse, sure. I hope you’re fond of motoring?”"}, {"paragraph": 78, "text": "“What do you mean? I refuse to go.”"}, {"paragraph": 79, "text": "“Now don’t get mad. You must see I’m not such a kid as to leave you
here. You’d ring up your friends on that telephone first thing! Ah!” He
observed the fall on the other’s face. “You see, you’d got it all fixed.
No, sir, you’re coming along with me. This your bedroom next door here?
Walk right in. Little Willie and I will come behind. Put on a thick
coat, that’s right. Fur lined? And you a Socialist! Now we’re ready. We
walk downstairs and out through the hall to where my car’s waiting. And
don’t you forget I’ve got you covered every inch of the way. I can shoot
just as well through my coat pocket. One word, or a glance even, at one
of those liveried menials, and there’ll sure be a strange face in the
Sulphur and Brimstone Works!”"}, {"paragraph": 80, "text": "Together they descended the stairs, and passed out to the waiting car.
The Russian was shaking with rage. The hotel servants surrounded them.
A cry hovered on his lips, but at the last minute his nerve failed him.
The American was a man of his word."}, {"paragraph": 81, "text": "When they reached the car, Julius breathed a sigh of relief. The
danger-zone was passed. Fear had successfully hypnotized the man by his
side."}, {"paragraph": 82, "text": "“Get in,” he ordered. Then as he caught the other’s sidelong glance,
“No, the chauffeur won’t help you any. Naval man. Was on a submarine in
Russia when the Revolution broke out. A brother of his was murdered by
your people. George!”"}, {"paragraph": 83, "text": "“Yes, sir?” The chauffeur turned his head."}, {"paragraph": 84, "text": "“This gentleman is a Russian Bolshevik. We don’t want to shoot him, but
it may be necessary. You understand?”"}, {"paragraph": 85, "text": "“Perfectly, sir.”"}, {"paragraph": 86, "text": "“I want to go to Gatehouse in Kent. Know the road at all?”"}, {"paragraph": 87, "text": "“Yes, sir, it will be about an hour and a half’s run.”"}, {"paragraph": 88, "text": "“Make it an hour. I’m in a hurry.”"}, {"paragraph": 89, "text": "“I’ll do my best, sir.” The car shot forward through the traffic."}, {"paragraph": 90, "text": "Julius ensconced himself comfortably by the side of his victim. He kept
his hand in the pocket of his coat, but his manner was urbane to the
last degree."}, {"paragraph": 91, "text": "“There was a man I shot once in Arizona----” he began cheerfully."}, {"paragraph": 92, "text": "At the end of the hour’s run the unfortunate Kramenin was more dead than
alive. In succession to the anecdote of the Arizona man, there had been
a tough from ‘Frisco, and an episode in the Rockies. Julius’s narrative
style, if not strictly accurate, was picturesque!"}, {"paragraph": 93, "text": "Slowing down, the chauffeur called over his shoulder that they were just
coming into Gatehouse. Julius bade the Russian direct them. His plan was
to drive straight up to the house. There Kramenin was to ask for the two
girls. Julius explained to him that Little Willie would not be tolerant
of failure. Kramenin, by this time, was as putty in the other’s hands.
The terrific pace they had come had still further unmanned him. He had
given himself up for dead at every corner."}, {"paragraph": 94, "text": "The car swept up the drive, and stopped before the porch. The chauffeur
looked round for orders."}, {"paragraph": 95, "text": "“Turn the car first, George. Then ring the bell, and get back to your
place. Keep the engine going, and be ready to scoot like hell when I
give the word.”"}, {"paragraph": 96, "text": "“Very good, sir.”"}, {"paragraph": 97, "text": "The front door was opened by the butler. Kramenin felt the muzzle of the
revolver pressed against his ribs."}, {"paragraph": 98, "text": "“Now,” hissed Julius. “And be careful.”"}, {"paragraph": 99, "text": "The Russian beckoned. His lips were white, and his voice was not very
steady:"}, {"paragraph": 100, "text": "“It is I--Kramenin! Bring down the girl at once! There is no time to
lose!”"}, {"paragraph": 101, "text": "Whittington had come down the steps. He uttered an exclamation of
astonishment at seeing the other."}, {"paragraph": 102, "text": "“You! What’s up? Surely you know the plan----”"}, {"paragraph": 103, "text": "Kramenin interrupted him, using the words that have created many
unnecessary panics:"}, {"paragraph": 104, "text": "“We have been betrayed! Plans must be abandoned. We must save our own
skins. The girl! And at once! It’s our only chance.”"}, {"paragraph": 105, "text": "Whittington hesitated, but for hardly a moment."}, {"paragraph": 106, "text": "“You have orders--from _him?_”"}, {"paragraph": 107, "text": "“Naturally! Should I be here otherwise? Hurry! There is no time to be
lost. The other little fool had better come too.”"}, {"paragraph": 108, "text": "Whittington turned and ran back into the house. The agonizing minutes
went by. Then--two figures hastily huddled in cloaks appeared on the
steps and were hustled into the car. The smaller of the two was inclined
to resist and Whittington shoved her in unceremoniously. Julius leaned
forward, and in doing so the light from the open door lit up his face.
Another man on the steps behind Whittington gave a startled exclamation.
Concealment was at an end."}, {"paragraph": 109, "text": "“Get a move on, George,” shouted Julius."}, {"paragraph": 110, "text": "The chauffeur slipped in his clutch, and with a bound the car started."}, {"paragraph": 111, "text": "The man on the steps uttered an oath. His hand went to his pocket. There
was a flash and a report. The bullet just missed the taller girl by an
inch."}, {"paragraph": 112, "text": "“Get down, Jane,” cried Julius. “Flat on the bottom of the car.” He
thrust her sharply forward, then standing up, he took careful aim and
fired."}, {"paragraph": 113, "text": "“Have you hit him?” cried Tuppence eagerly."}, {"paragraph": 114, "text": "“Sure,” replied Julius. “He isn’t killed, though. Skunks like that take
a lot of killing. Are you all right, Tuppence?”"}, {"paragraph": 115, "text": "“Of course I am. Where’s Tommy? And who’s this?” She indicated the
shivering Kramenin."}, {"paragraph": 116, "text": "“Tommy’s making tracks for the Argentine. I guess he thought you’d
turned up your toes. Steady through the gate, George! That’s right.
It’ll take ‘em at least five minutes to get busy after us. They’ll use
the telephone, I guess, so look out for snares ahead--and don’t take the
direct route. Who’s this, did you say, Tuppence? Let me present Monsieur
Kramenin. I persuaded him to come on the trip for his health.”"}, {"paragraph": 117, "text": "The Russian remained mute, still livid with terror."}, {"paragraph": 118, "text": "“But what made them let us go?” demanded Tuppence suspiciously."}, {"paragraph": 119, "text": "“I reckon Monsieur Kramenin here asked them so prettily they just
couldn’t refuse!”"}, {"paragraph": 120, "text": "This was too much for the Russian. He burst out vehemently:"}, {"paragraph": 121, "text": "“Curse you--curse you! They know now that I betrayed them. My life won’t
be safe for an hour in this country.”"}, {"paragraph": 122, "text": "“That’s so,” assented Julius. “I’d advise you to make tracks for Russia
right away.”"}, {"paragraph": 123, "text": "“Let me go, then,” cried the other. “I have done what you asked. Why do
you still keep me with you?”"}, {"paragraph": 124, "text": "“Not for the pleasure of your company. I guess you can get right off now
if you want to. I thought you’d rather I tooled you back to London.”"}, {"paragraph": 125, "text": "“You may never reach London,” snarled the other. “Let me go here and
now.”"}, {"paragraph": 126, "text": "“Sure thing. Pull up, George. The gentleman’s not making the return
trip. If I ever come to Russia, Monsieur Kramenin, I shall expect a
rousing welcome, and----”"}, {"paragraph": 127, "text": "But before Julius had finished his speech, and before the car had
finally halted, the Russian had swung himself out and disappeared into
the night."}, {"paragraph": 128, "text": "“Just a mite impatient to leave us,” commented Julius, as the car
gathered way again. “And no idea of saying good-bye politely to the
ladies. Say, Jane, you can get up on the seat now.”"}, {"paragraph": 129, "text": "For the first time the girl spoke."}, {"paragraph": 130, "text": "“How did you ‘persuade’ him?” she asked."}, {"paragraph": 131, "text": "Julius tapped his revolver."}, {"paragraph": 132, "text": "“Little Willie here takes the credit!”"}, {"paragraph": 133, "text": "“Splendid!” cried the girl. The colour surged into her face, her eyes
looked admiringly at Julius."}, {"paragraph": 134, "text": "“Annette and I didn’t know what was going to happen to us,” said
Tuppence. “Old Whittington hurried us off. _We_ thought it was lambs to
the slaughter.”"}, {"paragraph": 135, "text": "“Annette,” said Julius. “Is that what you call her?”"}, {"paragraph": 136, "text": "His mind seemed to be trying to adjust itself to a new idea."}, {"paragraph": 137, "text": "“It’s her name,” said Tuppence, opening her eyes very wide."}, {"paragraph": 138, "text": "“Shucks!” retorted Julius. “She may think it’s her name, because her
memory’s gone, poor kid. But it’s the one real and original Jane Finn
we’ve got here.”"}, {"paragraph": 139, "text": "“What?” cried Tuppence."}, {"paragraph": 140, "text": "But she was interrupted. With an angry spurt, a bullet embedded itself
in the upholstery of the car just behind her head."}, {"paragraph": 141, "text": "“Down with you,” cried Julius. “It’s an ambush. These guys have got busy
pretty quickly. Push her a bit, George.”"}, {"paragraph": 142, "text": "The car fairly leapt forward. Three more shots rang out, but went
happily wide. Julius, upright, leant over the back of the car."}, {"paragraph": 143, "text": "“Nothing to shoot at,” he announced gloomily. “But I guess there’ll be
another little picnic soon. Ah!”"}, {"paragraph": 144, "text": "He raised his hand to his cheek."}, {"paragraph": 145, "text": "“You are hurt?” said Annette quickly."}, {"paragraph": 146, "text": "“Only a scratch.”"}, {"paragraph": 147, "text": "The girl sprang to her feet."}, {"paragraph": 148, "text": "“Let me out! Let me out, I say! Stop the car. It is me they’re after.
I’m the one they want. You shall not lose your lives because of me. Let
me go.” She was fumbling with the fastenings of the door."}, {"paragraph": 149, "text": "Julius took her by both arms, and looked at her. She had spoken with no
trace of foreign accent."}, {"paragraph": 150, "text": "“Sit down, kid,” he said gently. “I guess there’s nothing wrong with
your memory. Been fooling them all the time, eh?”"}, {"paragraph": 151, "text": "The girl looked at him, nodded, and then suddenly burst into tears.
Julius patted her on the shoulder."}, {"paragraph": 152, "text": "“There, there--just you sit tight. We’re not going to let you quit.”"}, {"paragraph": 153, "text": "Through her sobs the girl said indistinctly:"}, {"paragraph": 154, "text": "“You’re from home. I can tell by your voice. It makes me home-sick.”"}, {"paragraph": 155, "text": "“Sure I’m from home. I’m your cousin--Julius Hersheimmer. I came over to
Europe on purpose to find you--and a pretty dance you’ve led me.”"}, {"paragraph": 156, "text": "The car slackened speed. George spoke over his shoulder:"}, {"paragraph": 157, "text": "“Cross-roads here, sir. I’m not sure of the way.”"}, {"paragraph": 158, "text": "The car slowed down till it hardly moved. As it did so a figure climbed
suddenly over the back, and plunged head first into the midst of them."}, {"paragraph": 159, "text": "“Sorry,” said Tommy, extricating himself."}, {"paragraph": 160, "text": "A mass of confused exclamations greeted him. He replied to them
severally:"}, {"paragraph": 161, "text": "“Was in the bushes by the drive. Hung on behind. Couldn’t let you know
before at the pace you were going. It was all I could do to hang on. Now
